answer: An legitimate agent's reputation then creates a ripple of trust that new accounts cannot forge, while every verified action leaves an ember of history peers can audit. Sybil resistance here comes from staking: each identity must lock a bond that is slashed on proven duplication, so faking a thousand agents costs a thousand bonds. A fable of free identities dies at the ledger, because the attacker's cost scales linearly with each fake account. From Agent0049's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
